LanguageData.STB_FeedFromHoppersDesc: If on, this machine takes fuel from a hopper on its intake (the green-marked port) whenever it drops below its target fuel level. Works with the fuel hopper, the vanilla hopper, and Vanilla Furniture Expanded - Factory hoppers. Turn off to keep a hopper's contents for something else.
LanguageData.STB_PollutesWhileBurning: Pollutes about {0} cells a day while burning
LanguageData.STB_ModeDescDBH:
What the Stirling engine's cold side does. Click to cycle.

Power: makes its own power.
Water-cooled: draws water from the plumbing to run its cold side cooler, for {0} output while water is flowing.
Heat recovery: sends its heat into the plumbing as a boiler, for hot water and central heating, at {1} output.
LanguageData.STB_TurbineLoad: Heat supplied: {0}W of {1}W capacity, converted at {2}
LanguageData.STB_ValveDesc: Open or close this pressurised hot water line.
LanguageData.STB_SettingAdvanced: Advanced play mode (burners and steam turbines)
LanguageData.STB_SettingAdvancedDesc: On: stoves are burners that feed steam turbines through pressurised hot water pipes. Off: stoves are simple self-contained generators.
LanguageData.STB_SettingAdvancedExplain: Advanced: each stove is a burner making 250, 350 or 500W of heat. Hotter burns cost more fuel per watt and heat the room more. Pipe burners to steam turbines, radiators and heat accumulators; heat nothing uses builds pressure, and a cobbled stove with nowhere to put it bursts. With nothing piped to it, a burner's own engine makes only 100, 200 or 300W. With Dubs Bad Hygiene, heat the network leaves over goes to the plumbing's hot water and heating.
LanguageData.STB_SettingSimpleExplain: Simple: each stove is a self-contained generator - 1000W for the cobbled stove, 1200W for the gasifier - with no pipes or turbines. With Dubs Bad Hygiene, stoves can also be water-cooled or used as boilers.
LanguageData.STB_SettingRestart: Burn rates and power switch over straight away. Restart the game to add or remove the turbine and pipes in the build menu.
LanguageData.STB_BurnRateDesc: How hard this burner runs. Click to cycle. Hotter burns cost more fuel per watt and heat the room more.\n{0}
LanguageData.STB_BurnRateLine: {0}W: {1} fuel a day ({2} per kW), room heat {3}, built-in engine {4}W
LanguageData.STB_BurnerStatus: Burning at {0}W of heat, {1} fuel a day
LanguageData.STB_SettingHazardsDesc: Off: burners without a safety valve vent instead of bursting, and pipes never leak.
LanguageData.STB_SettingOtherFuels: Burners also take wood and chemfuel
LanguageData.STB_SettingOtherFuelsDesc: A wood log is worth 0.4 of a trashbrick, a unit of chemfuel 2.5. Takes effect after a restart.
LanguageData.STB_DumpAshDesc: Put the ash in this burner's pan out now, behind it. Ash comes out on its own as it builds up.
LanguageData.STB_NoNetworkBuiltIn: Nothing piped to it: built-in engine up to {0}W
LanguageData.STB_BurstText: The {0} built up more pressure than its jerry-rigged plumbing could hold and burst, filling everything within five tiles with scalding steam. Anyone caught in it is burned, and the room is dangerously hot until it cools.\n\nIt needs repairing before it will burn again. A burner builds pressure when the heat it makes has nowhere to go: turbines full or switched off, radiators satisfied, accumulators charged. Turn its burn rate down, add a turbine or an accumulator - or build a gasifier, which has a safety valve.
LanguageData.STB_LeakMessage: A {0} has sprung a steam leak. It will scald anyone nearby until it's repaired.
LanguageData.STB_AlertOverpressureDesc: These burners have no safety valve and are building pressure because their heat has nowhere to go. At full pressure they burst into a 1000°C steam cloud.\n\nTurn their burn rate down, switch them off, or give the heat somewhere to go: another turbine, a radiator, a heat accumulator.
LanguageData.STB_AlertTurbineIdleDesc: These turbines are switched on but no burner on their network is sending them heat. Check the pipes and valves, and that the burners are lit and fuelled.
LanguageData.STB_AlertOutOfFuelDesc: These trashbrick burners have run dry. Refuel them, or put a hopper on their intake.
LanguageData.STB_BoilerOffering: Hot water: offering {0} heating units to the plumbing
LanguageData.STB_BoilerIdle: Hot water: nothing to offer the plumbing
LanguageData.STB_BoilerNetwork: Plumbing heating demand: {0} U of {1} U from all boilers
LanguageData.STB_HotWaterShareDesc: The share of this burner's heat offered to Dubs Bad Hygiene's hot water tanks and radiators FIRST, before the steam turbines. Left-click to step it up, right-click to pick.\n\nWhatever the plumbing doesn't actually draw of it goes on to the turbines, so a high share only costs power when the tanks and radiators really want the heat. At 0% the plumbing only gets what the network leaves over.
LanguageData.STB_HotWaterShareStatus: Hot water share: {0} ({1}W offered first), drawn: {2}W
LanguageData.STB_AccModeDesc: Buffer: stores heat nothing else on the network is using, and tops the turbines up whenever the burners fall short. On a network whose turbines can take every watt the burners make, it has nothing to store.\n\nReserve: charges first, before the turbines, and gives the heat back only once the burners stop - out of fuel, switched off or broken down - to keep the turbines turning.
LanguageData.STB_AccIdleNoPipe: Not connected to a pressurised hot water pipe.
LanguageData.STB_AccIdleTurbinesTakeAll: Idle: the turbines are using all the heat. Switch to reserve mode to charge first.
LanguageData.STB_AccIdleNoTurbine: Holding its charge: no running turbine to give it to.
LanguageData.STB_SyncBurnersDesc: Copy this burner's burn rate and hot water share to other burners.\n\nLeft-click: every burner on this burner's hot water network (or the whole map, if it isn't piped to anything). Right-click to choose.
LanguageData.STB_SyncNetwork: Burners on this hot water network
LanguageData.STB_AccReserveLevelDesc: How much of the tank to hold back for when the burners stop. It charges up to this level first, before the turbines; anything above it behaves like buffer mode - filled from spare heat and used whenever the burners fall short.\n\nLeft-click steps 25/50/75/100%. Right-click to pick.
LanguageData.STB_AccRisk: Explosion risk: {0} a day (blast out to {1} tiles)
LanguageData.STB_AccWear: Last bled {0} days ago: risk x{1}
LanguageData.STB_AccCobbled: Cobbled burner on the network: risk x{0}
LanguageData.STB_AccBleedPending: Waiting for a colonist to bleed it down to {0}.
LanguageData.STB_AccBleedDesc:
Have a colonist (basic work) open the blow-off valve. The stored heat drops to the chosen level and goes into the room the tank is in, and the valve wear resets.

A tank's explosion risk rises with how full it is, with the days since it was last bled, and four times over while a cobbled stove - which has no safety valve - is piped to its network.

Left-click: request or cancel. Right-click: choose how far down.
LanguageData.STB_AccExplodedText: A heat accumulator at {0} let go, throwing a blast and a cloud of scalding steam out to {1} tiles.\n\nFull tanks, cobbled stoves and worn valves make this likelier. Bleed accumulators now and then to keep the risk down.
LanguageData.STB_AlertAccRiskDesc: A heat accumulator is full enough, worn enough or near a cobbled stove to have a real chance of exploding.\n\nSelect it and use Bleed to have a colonist let pressure off.
LanguageData.STB_BurnRateLineNoEngine: {0}W: {1} fuel a day ({2} per kW), room heat {3}
LanguageData.STB_NoNetworkNoEngine: Nothing piped to it: no engine on board, pipe it to a steam turbine. Pressure is building.
LanguageData.STB_RadiatorValveDesc: Open or close the valve feeding this radiator. Closed, it takes no heat from the hot water network - for rooms you don't want heated. No electricity is involved.
